newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL-Tambrands, disk drive makers rise.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL-Tambrands, disk drive makers rise.

text.p: Shares of Tambrands Inc rose in pre-opening trading on Wednesday after it received and accepted a $50 a share cash bid from Procter & Gamble Co, traders said.
Disk drive-makers were also higher after Seagate Technology Inc posted stronger-than-expected third quarter earnings.
Procter & Gamble moved higher, to 116-3/8 from its Tuesday New York Stock Exchange close of 115-7/8. Tambrands shot up to 48-3/4, up 2-1/2, traders said.

Procter & Gamble announced earlier it would buy Tambrands for $50 a share or $1.85 billion, but traders said rumors of a deal had been circulating for some time before the announcement, sending the activity of Tambrands options into overdrive.
Quantum Corp and Read-Rite Corp were higher after rival disk drive maker Seagate Technology posted third quarter earnings that blew away Wall Street estimates.

The company earned $1.01 a share for the third quarter ended March 28, 1997 including certain charges. Without the charges, earning per share would have been $1.07. First Call consensus estimates were not immediately available.

Seagate shares were being bid at 53, up from their close at 51-1/2, traders said. Quantum shares moved up 7/8 to 47 from their close at 46-1/8 and Read-Rite shares were bid at 33, up from their close at 32-5/8.
Also sharply higher was HBO & Co, which jumped more than five to 55 after the company posted first quarter earnings per share of $0.38.
"They were expected to miss their number, but they came in okay," said one trader.
Vivus Inc was also higher, bid at 48-3/4, up seven, after its first quarter profits more than doubled Wall Street estimates. The company makes a treatment for male impotence.
